name: OW-BUILD-the-host-never-says-the-view-is-up
note: The Overworld's ground comes at the 60-a-second frame's pace: the report's x1 on every machine that cannot keep up.

name: OW-LAG-the-view-alone
note: OW-BUILD as it shipped: every frame under the view drops to 30 a second while anything is queued - the report.

name: OW-LAG-the-view-forgotten
note: A word left from the view's last frame lends the Overworld's slice on the ground.

name: OW-LAG-the-word-never-kept
note: The governor's word dropped: the Overworld never builds faster, OW-BUILD undone.

name: OW-LAG-the-count-ignored
note: Any fast travel under the view takes the frame to 30 a second, the ground keeping up or not.

name: OW-LAG-the-enemies-ignored
note: An enemy holding the clock to x1 still costs the frame its rate for a build that lifts nothing.

name: OW-LAG-an-exit-answers-undefined
note: THE MODAL CONTRACT broken: one exit answers undefined where the rest answer a boolean.

name: OW-BUILD-sized-against-the-display
note: The display's frame, not the Overworld's: a 60 Hz screen leaves the stream its ordinary slice and a 144 Hz one the same, the view changing nothing.

name: OW-BUILD-sixty-a-second
note: The Overworld's frame at 60 a second: the slice no bigger than the ordinary one on a light frame.

name: OW-BUILD-no-cap
old: return Number.isNaN(left) ? BUILD_SLICE_MS : Math.max(BUILD_SLICE_MS, Math.min(BUILD_SLICE_OVERWORLD_MS, left));
note: A light frame lends the stream 30 ms and the view drops under 30 a second.

name: OW-BUILD-the-prover-floor-under-the-view
old: return Number.isNaN(left) ? BUILD_SLICE_MS : Math.max(BUILD_SLICE_MS, Math.min(BUILD_SLICE_OVERWORLD_MS, left));
new: return Number.isNaN(left) ? BUILD_SLICE_MS : Math.max(BUILD_SLICE_FLOOR_MS, Math.min(BUILD_SLICE_OVERWORLD_MS, left));
note: A heavy frame under the view gets 3 ms where an old stream had 6: the Overworld builds slower than the ground it replaced.

name: OW-BUILD-a-NaN-stalls
old: return Number.isNaN(left) ? BUILD_SLICE_MS : Math.max(BUILD_SLICE_MS, Math.min(BUILD_SLICE_OVERWORLD_MS, left));
note: A NaN busy reading answers NaN, and the breather yields every breath.
